title.title: The work of Władysław Narkiewicz in number theory and related areas

editorial_contributions.text:
The authors define a ``base \(b\) large digit'' as a digit (one of the numbers \(0,1,\ldots, b-1\)) not less than \(b/2\), and the remaining digits are called ``small base \(b\) digits''. The method of \textit{W. Narkiewicz} [Publ. Elektroteh. Fak., Univ. Beogr., Ser. Mat. Fiz. 678-715, 173-174 (1980; Zbl 0457.10003)] is generalized, and the following result is proved. Let \(L_b(m)\) denote the number of base \(b\) large digits of the base \(b\) representation of \(m\). Let further \(a\) and \(b\) be fixed natural numbers with \((a,b)=1\), \(S(x)\) denote the number of integers \(n\) not exceeding \(x\) such that \(L_b(a^n)=0\), \(\beta\) are the number of integers \(d\) less than \(b\), coprime with \(b\), such that \(d\) is ``small'', and \(\theta=20\log(\frac{b+1}2)/\log b\). If \(\varphi\) is Euler's function, then 
\[
 S(x)\leq\beta\Bigl(\frac{b(1-\theta)}{\theta\varphi(b)}\Bigr)^\theta \Bigl(\frac 1{1-\theta}\Bigr)x^\theta. .
\]

title.title: A generalization of a result by Narkiewicz concerning large digits of powers

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(K\) be an algebraic field and \(\mathbb Z_K\) its ring of integers. A number \(\beta\in \mathbb Z_K\) is said to generate a canonical number system (\textit{CNS}) if every \(\alpha\in \mathbb Z_K\) can be written in the form 
\[
\alpha = \sum_{j=0}^k c_j\beta^j,\tag{1}
\]
where \(k\) depends on \(\alpha\) and \(0\le c_j< |N(\beta)|-1\) (the digits of \(\alpha\)) are rational integers. It has been shown by \textit{B. Kovacs} [Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hung. 37, 405--407 (1981; Zbl 0505.12001)] that (\textit{CNS}) exists in \(K\) if and only if \(K\) is monogenic.

Theorem 1.5 of the paper states that if \(\beta\) generates a (\textit{CNS}), is not divisible by a ramified prime ideal and the ideals generated by \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are relatively prime, then for the number \(\mathcal M_b(\alpha,\beta,x)\) of integers \(n\le x\) such that in the expansion (1) of \(\alpha^n\) a fixed digit \(b\) does not appear, then
\[
\mathcal M_b(\alpha,\beta,x)\le c(\beta)x^{\sigma(\beta)},
\]
with \(\sigma(\beta)=\frac{\log(x)-1}{\log(x)}\).

Earlier this has been known only in the elementary case with \(K=\mathbb Q\), \(\beta=3\), \(\alpha =2\) [the reviewer, Publ. Elektroteh. Fak., Univ. Beogr., Ser. Mat. Fiz. 678--715, 173--174 (1980; Zbl 0457.10003)].

In Theorem 1.8 a similar result is proved for infinite \(\beta\)-expansions
\[
\alpha = \sum_{j=0}^\infty c_j\beta^j,
\]
with \(c_j\) lying in a fixed set of residues mod \(\beta\). This series is convergent in completions \(K_\mathfrak p\) with respect to prime ideals \(\mathfrak p\) dividing \(\beta\).

Reviewer's remark: One has to assume additionally that \(\alpha\) is not a root of unity, as otherwise the expression given by the formula (4.5) may vanish. Actually, if \(\alpha\) is a root of unity, then \(\mathcal M_b(\alpha,\beta,x)\) either vanishes for all \(x\) or equals \((A(b)+o(1))x)\) with \(A(b)>0\). Moreover the presented proof does not cover the case when the omitted digit equals zero.

editorial_contributions.text:
Among the notable consequences of the \textit{squarefree conjecture}, proposed by Paul Erdős, Ronald L. Graham, I. Z. Ruzsa and E. G. Straus [\textit{P. Erdős} et al., Math. Comput. 29, 83--92 (1975; Zbl 0296.10008)] and established by \textit{A. Granville} and \textit{O. Ramaré} [Mathematika 43, No. 1, 73--107 (1996; Zbl 0868.11009)], there are the two open problems (illustrated, respectively, by Ronald L. Graham, Donald E. Knuth and Oren Patashnik [\textit{R. L. Graham} et al., Concrete mathematics: a foundation for computer science. 2nd ed. Amsterdam: Addison-Wesley Publishing Group (1994; Zbl 0836.00001) and by \textit{Paul Erdős} [Math. Mag. 52, 67--70 (1979; Zbl 0407.10001)] and) inspiring this paper.


The periodicity of the base \(p\) representation of the numbers in the form \(\alpha^k\), where \(p\) is a prime and \((\alpha, p)=1\), leads to an upper bound (whose search allows to refine similar results from \textit{R. E. Kennedy} and \textit{C. Cooper} [Publ. Elektroteh. Fak., Univ. Beogr., Ser. Mat. 11, 36--40 (2000; Zbl 0999.11008)] and from \textit{W. Narkiewicz} [Publ. Elektroteh. Fak., Univ. Beogr., Ser. Mat. Fiz. 678--715, 173--174 (1980; Zbl 0457.10003)]) on the number of \(k\)'s less than \(a\) such that \((\alpha^k)_p\) contains less than \(n\) digits bigger than \(\frac{p}{2}\) for every \(n\) and \(a\). Via a well known theorem of \textit{E. E. Kummer} [J. Reine Angew. Math. 44, 93--146 (1852; Zbl 02750589)], the authors find a null asymptotic density for the set of integers \(k\) such that \(m \nmid \binom{2^{k+1}}{2^k}\) for every odd \(m\) and they hypothesize there is a positive integer \(h\) such that \(m \nmid \binom{2^{k+1}}{2^k}\) for every \(k>h\).

The paper is enriched by an interesting digression about the Wieferich primes (explored by \textit{W. Keller} and \textit{J. Richstein} [Math. Comput. 74, No. 250, 927--936 (2005; Zbl 1137.11301)]) and by a source code checking that the central binomial coefficient \(\binom{2n}{n}\) is divisible by \(4\) or \(9\) for every \(n\) such that \(4<n \leq 2^{{10}^{13}}\) except for \(n=64\) and \(n=256\); it enlarges the interval supplied by \textit{P. Goetgheluck} [Math. Comput. 51, No. 183, 325--329 (1988; Zbl 0673.10012)].
